extracted.intended_audience: improvisers, improv teachers, and students of long-form improv
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and a short rubric for evaluating or producing improvised scenes (especially long-form Harold-style work), emphasizing honesty, pattern recognition, ensemble play, and structural tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Players being honest and brave (no jokey deflection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are players being honest and brave (no jokey deflection)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Play scenes realistically with honesty, bravery, and integrity; avoid jokey deflection or reaching for obvious jokes. Authentic choices fuel scene truth and comedic payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern Recognition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice what's emerging in a scene and spot the unusual thing. Patterns are inherently satisfying — subverting or amplifying them creates humor. Rather than relying on jokes, emphasize pattern recognition and subversion of expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group Mind / Ensemble
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the group mind operating (no upstaging)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Players think and react as one ensemble; contributions support the whole. Do not upstage or pursue individual spotlight at the expense of the group's direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Yes, And' / Offers Accepted
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accept everything offered and add to it. Build on partners' offers rather than negating or blocking them; 'yes, and' keeps momentum and generates material to be patterned or recalled later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene remembers earlier elements
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-form improv should 'remember' earlier details and callbacks. Use previously introduced elements to create connections across beats and scenes — "non-linear entertainment that remembers everything."

rubrics_metrics.name: Nothing is wasted
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid extraneous lines or actions; every offer should be usable later as part of pattern building or callbacks. 'Wastes nothing' means material should either advance character/relationship/emerging pattern or be available for later payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Harold (Long Form) structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Harold: six to seven players; many scenes (games, monologues, songs, skits); three sets of three scenes interleaved with group games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Harold's non-linear, interleaved structure to develop multiple threads that can be remembered and recombined. The structure encourages pattern recognition, callbacks, and ensemble awareness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of improvisational tools (Pattern Game, Hot Spot, The Harold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tools: The Pattern Game; Hot Spot; The Harold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ named exercises and formats (Pattern Game, Hot Spot, The Harold) to surface patterns, focus ensemble attention, and generate material suited for long-form interconnection and payoff.
